marks.gloss_en: תניא כוותיה דרבא
the baraita, R' Yehuda: no doors at all, because the child grows over-confident and may put out his head; rather Egyptian oxen with broad bellies
והרי מטה דיש בה כמה אגרופים, ותנן רבי יהודה אומר: נוהגים היינו שהיינו ישנים תחת המטה! -- a bed has several fistbreadths, yet R' Yehuda does not treat it as a tent
שאני מטה, הואיל ולגבה עשויה (= p_mita_legabah; countered by obj_shvarim_legaban)
שוורים נמי לגבן עשויים! -- oxen too are made for use on top of them (an attack on the answer שאני מטה; header)
the stam: a bed is different, since it is made for [use] on top of it
ואיבעית אימא: R' Yehuda follows his view that the sukkah is a permanent dwelling, and a temporary tent does not negate a permanent one (= p_yehuda_letaameh)
R' Yehuda, as the stam cites him: we require a sukkah that is a permanent dwelling
Ravin in R' Elazar's name: oxen shelter the shepherds from sun and rain (= p_elazar_meginim, itself refuted by obj_mita_meginah)
אי הכי, מטה נמי — הואיל ומגינה על מנעלים וסנדלים שתחתיה! -- unanswered; Rava's אלא replaces R' Elazar's distinction
R' Elazar (via Ravin): oxen are different, since they shelter the shepherds from the sun and from the rain
אלא אמר רבא: oxen are made to protect their own innards, שנאמר עור ובשר תלבישני (= p_rava_bnei_meayim)
Rava: rather, oxen are different, since [their bodies] are made to protect their own innards
והא רבי שמעון דאמר נמי סוכה דירת קבע בעינן, ואתי אהל עראי ומבטל אהל קבע! -- dirat keva alone does not explain R' Yehuda
אין, בהא פליגי -- they dispute exactly whether a temporary tent negates a permanent one (= p_bhai_pligi)
R' Shimon, as the stam cites him: he too requires a sukkah that is a permanent dwelling
R' Shimon: from Rabban Gamliel's conversation we learned two things
even the conversation of Torah scholars requires study
one who supports his sukkah on the legs of a bed -- it is valid
one said: [R' Yehuda invalidates it] because it has no permanence
what is between them? where he wedged in iron skewers and roofed over them
Abaye: they taught [the dispute] only where he leaned [the sukkah on the bed]
